title: PostgreSQL Connection Pool Exhaustion
symptoms: Application logs report 'Timeout acquiring connection from pool'
Database active connections reach max_connections limit
Cascading 500/504 errors in dependent upstream APIs
remediation_steps: 1. Inspect active connection count via `SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity;`
2. Terminate long-running idle in transaction queries: `SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state = 'idle in transaction' AND state_change < now() - INTERVAL '5 minutes';`
3. Scale PgBouncer pool size or increase application max-pool-size.
4. Restart connection pooler service to release leaked handles.
verification_steps: Verify connection pool utilization falls below 70%
Confirm API response latencies return to p95 < 200ms

title: Worker Process Heap Memory Leak & OOM Crash
symptoms: Monotonically rising memory usage over time without plateau
Elevated Garbage Collection (GC) pauses causing request queueing
Container terminated with OOMKilled (Exit Code 137)
remediation_steps: 1. Trigger an on-demand heap dump before container recycling if diagnostics enabled.
2. Perform graceful rolling restart of the affected worker deployment.
3. Temporarily increase container memory limit by 50% in Kubernetes deployment manifest.
4. Roll back recent commits touching in-memory caches or object references.
verification_steps: Monitor resident set size (RSS) memory stabilization after restart
Ensure container restart count stops incrementing

title: Bad Deployment / Release Rollback
symptoms: Immediate surge in 500 errors starting within seconds of deployment event
SyntaxError, ImportError, or migration incompatibility logs
Health check endpoint failures on newly provisioned pods
remediation_steps: 1. Immediately execute deployment rollback to previous stable tag: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/<service-name>`
2. Invalidate deployment lock and stop ongoing CI/CD pipelines.
3. Verify previous stable image pods reach Ready 1/1 state.
4. Engage release author to triage faulty commit diff.
verification_steps: Confirm error rate drops back to baseline (< 0.1%)
Verify deployment revision matches last known stable hash

title: Disk Space Exhaustion & Write Failure
symptoms: I/O Error: 'No space left on device'
Log append failures and database write transaction aborts
System services crashing due to inability to write pid or temp files
remediation_steps: 1. Identify offending mount and directory: `df -h` and `du -sh /var/log/*`
2. Truncate unrotated or oversized log files: `truncate -s 0 /var/log/app/*.log`
3. Clean temporary directories: `rm -rf /tmp/*.tmp`
4. Trigger volume resize / expand Persistent Volume Claim (PVC).
verification_steps: Confirm available disk space is > 20% on all critical mounts

title: Redis Cache Eviction Storm & Saturation
symptoms: High rate of evicted keys reported in Redis INFO stats
Severe latency degradation on database due to cache miss stampede
Cache client connection timeouts
remediation_steps: 1. Check Redis memory usage: `redis-cli info memory`
2. Increase maxmemory limit or scale Redis cluster shards.
3. Temporarily enable circuit-breaking on expensive cache-aside queries.
4. Review keyspace expiration policies (switch to volatile-lru if appropriate).
verification_steps: Confirm cache hit ratio recovers above 90%

title: API Gateway & Egress Network Timeout
symptoms: API Gateway returning 504 Gateway Timeout to external clients
Upstream connection refused or socket read timeout errors
Degraded ingress throughput
remediation_steps: 1. Check connectivity to upstream service: `curl -v http://upstream-service:port/health`
2. Scale upstream service replicas if latency is caused by traffic overload.
3. Inspect service mesh / Envoy proxy logs for connection pool exhaustion.
4. Restart Envoy sidecar proxies if route tables are stale.
verification_steps: Verify gateway 504 rate drops to zero

title: Kafka Consumer Lag & Rebalance Loop
symptoms: Consumer lag continuously climbing across topic partitions
Frequent 'CommitFailedException' and repeated rebalance storms
Messages remaining unconsumed past SLA thresholds
remediation_steps: 1. Increase `max.poll.interval.ms` to give consumers adequate processing time.
2. Temporarily reduce `max.poll.records` to prevent timeout on batch processing.
3. Scale consumer group instances up to partition count.
4. Restart unresponsive consumer pods.
verification_steps: Confirm consumer lag trends downwards toward zero

title: Kubernetes Pod CrashLoopBackOff
symptoms: Pod status showing CrashLoopBackOff in `kubectl get pods`
Liveness probe consecutive failure threshold exceeded
Application failing during initialization
remediation_steps: 1. Inspect pod termination reason and logs: `kubectl describe pod <pod>` and `kubectl logs <pod> --previous`
2. Check for missing configuration secrets or broken configmaps.
3. Increase liveness probe `initialDelaySeconds` if cold boot is slow.
4. Restart deployment after applying fix.
verification_steps: Confirm all pods enter Running state with 1/1 containers Ready
Confirm restart count does not increment
